tier_reason: The only numbers are an independent but obscure single-run 2020 shootout (guteksan/REST-CPP-benchmark, 130 stars, 17 commits, compiler unstated) whose results table image shows cpp-httplib beating C++ REST SDK in just one of the six cells where both completed (Local N=1000 t=0 C=28, 3.015 s vs 3.401 s, 1.13x) and losing or tying in the other five (up to 1.88x slower over VPN), so it does not show the win B requires; public code, CPU model and CMake Release flags are present but the compiler is not, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Read from images/rest_all.PNG (time from first request received to last reply, 10 producers x N requests). Local, N=1000, t=0 ms, C=28: cpp-httplib v0.5.8 3.015 s vs C++ REST SDK 3.401 s (1.13x faster, derived from page data). In the other five cells where C++ REST SDK completed (all C=28) cpp-httplib is slower or tied: VPN N=1000 t=0 3:31.510 vs 1:52.476 (1.88x slower, derived from page data); Local N=200 t=200 40.359 s vs 40.281 s; Local N=1000 t=200 3:21.790 vs 3:21.415; VPN N=200 t=200 1:22.168 vs 1:01.523 (1.34x slower, derived from page data); VPN N=1000 t=200 6:51.648 vs 5:11.715 (1.32x slower, derived from page data). In all six C=4 cells C++ REST SDK deadlocked while cpp-httplib finished (e.g. 1.915 s at Local N=1000 t=0). In the Local sprint cell cpp-httplib is slower than Crow (1.536 s), Pistache (1.059 s), Restbed (1.333 s) and Restinio (1.025 s), and it is marked worst (red) in 7 of the 12 cells.
corrections.workload: Independent shootout (guteksan/REST-CPP-benchmark, 2020): 10 Python producer processes (postInLoop.py, http.client, a new TCP connection per request, printing under a shared lock) each POST N=200 or 1000 small JSON messages to a /test echo endpoint that sleeps t=0 or 200 ms; services use C=28 or C=4 worker threads and run Local (same machine) or over a VPN; metric is time from the service's first logged request reception to its last reply (log4cplus timestamps), one run per cell.
corrections.caveats: Weak and mostly unfavourable evidence. cpp-httplib's authors make no speed claim; the repo's benchmark/ directory builds a Crow v1.3.1 server beside cpp-httplib (Makefile bench-all, bombardier -c 10 -d 5s, -O2, CPPHTTPLIB_THREAD_POOL_COUNT=16) but publishes no numbers, and benchmark/ab.sh compares two cpp-httplib git refs, not another library; ab.sh itself warns that the same binary varies by +/-20% run to run, which covers the single 1.13x cell below. The only numbers found are third-party, from a small 2020 shootout (130 stars, all 17 commits in May-June 2020) testing cpp-httplib v0.5.8 and C++ REST SDK v2.10.15, both far older than the current v0.60.0 (released 2026-10-07). The win over C++ REST SDK holds in one cell only (Local, N=1000, t=0 ms, C=28: 3.015 s vs 3.401 s); in the matching VPN cell cpp-httplib is 1.88x slower (3:31.510 vs 1:52.476), it ties or trails in the Local t=200 ms cells and trails in every VPN C=28 cell; in the C=4 cells it 'wins' only because C++ REST SDK deadlocks when threads are fewer than producers. It is slower than Crow, Pistache, Restbed and Restinio in the sprint cell and is marked worst in 7 of 12 cells; the shootout's analysis singles out its doubled VPN overhead (210 s per 1000 requests) and its large degradation at C=4. The shootout README's phrase that Restinio was over 3 times faster than 'the worst Cpp-REST-SDK followed by Httplib' ranks Httplib second-worst, which matches the table. Harness: Python client opening a new connection per request, server-side logging through log4cplus twice per request, about 10,000 requests per cell, a single run per cell with no repeats or variance; faster frameworks finish the same load in about 1 s, so the 3 s figures are server-bound rather than client-capped. The published basic-httplib/main.cpp leaves CPPHTTPLIB_THREAD_POOL_COUNT commented out, so the C=4 runs needed a recompile not in the repo. Numbers exist only as a table image; compiler and version not stated. The guessed baseline (OpenSSL) and category (tls) were wrong; the repo is an HTTP server and client library and was refiled under http-servers-frameworks.

notes: Real, very popular library (16.9k stars, MIT, active, v0.60.0 on 2026-10-07) but not shown faster than its baseline: of six completed comparisons against C++ REST SDK it wins one by 1.13x (single run, within its own repo's stated +/-20% noise), ties two and loses three (up to 1.88x slower), and it is the worst of six frameworks in 7 of 12 cells. Record shortcomings: not faster except one cell, obscure single-run 2020 shootout on v0.5.8, compiler unstated, baseline wins in C=4 cells only by deadlocking; the record's own caveats misread the VPN cell as the win and misread the README's 'followed by Httplib' wording, both fixed in the corrected caveats.
